Blocks.Text: As a partner, when an applicant submits a job application to your posted job on LinkedIn, LinkedIn creates a POST request to the webhook URL you have registered for that job posting.

In the payload, you will receive the job application ID. Ensure that you store this ID to further use it in the Applicant Highlights plugin, Apply Connect Full Profile plugin, and in the Job Application Feedback API.
Important
If the first application fails to deliver to your servers, the job will be converted to an off-site apply (on your website instead of LinkedIn) using the companyApplyUrl provided in the payload.

Respond to all LinkedIn validation requests. For more information, refer to webhook validation.
Verify the validity of push event requests using the x-li-signature. For more information, refer to webhook validation.
Return a 200 OK status code to indicate that the application is successfully received by your servers. LinkedIn will attempt to re-send the application 6 times if a non-200 status code is returned.
Create or supplement existing candidate application details from the delivered application response.
Mark the application source as "LinkedIn Easy Apply" in your system for tracking and analytics purposes.
Provide the associated errorCode and additionalErrorDetails for failed application delivery (non-200 HTTP response). For more information, refer to error handling.

LinkedIn generates webhook signatures using HMAC-SHA256 encryption with your application's secret key. The signature is calculated from the escaped unicode request payload, prefixed with hmacsha256=, and included in the X-LI-Signature header.

To validate incoming webhooks, compute your own HMAC-SHA256 signature using the same secret key and compare it against the X-LI-Signature header value. Add the prefix hmacsha256= to your signature for a complete match. Test your implementation using local tooling and standard cryptographic libraries in your programming language of choice—never expose your secret key or payload to third-party or online HMAC generators.
Important
The jobApplicationWebhookUrl is provided in the job payload when creating an OnsiteApplyConfigured job—no separate registration in the developer portal is required.
To ensure secure communication, all jobApplicationWebhookUrls must support the webhook endpoint validation flow, specified in Webhooks.

Blocks.Text: LinkedIn sends an applicationId query parameter with validation requests to indicate which application's clientSecret to use for generating the challenge response. Use the clientSecret associated with the child application specified in the applicationId parameter.
LinkedIn performs validation of webhook endpoints at the following times:

Initial validation: When a new jobApplicationWebhookUrl is first registered.
Re-validation: Every 2 hours after initial validation.
Manual validation: Can be triggered from the developer portal.
If re-validation fails 3 consecutive times, the endpoint will be blocked and events will no longer be sent.
You can verify the validation status of your webhook endpoint using any of the following methods:

Developer portal: Navigate to the Webhooks tab in your application, where blocked endpoints are displayed with a blocked status.
Email notifications: Review warning emails sent for failed validation attempts and the notification sent when the endpoint is blocked.
Challenge response: Successfully returning the correct challengeResponse during validation confirms the endpoint is validated.
Note
If validation fails, the job posting will be automatically converted to off-site apply, and you will stop receiving applications through the webhook.
POST https://{jobApplicationWebhookUrl}

Currently, this list will contain explicit skills listed by the applicant on their LinkedIn profile that match the job posting's standardized skills, as well as all skills for which an applicant has completed a skill assessment, regardless of whether that skill matches the job posting's standardized skills. Blocks.Text: The mediaUrl will be returned when the applicant uploads a resume, cover letter, or additional files with their job application. This media is short-lived and will be available for 30 days. This url can be accessed and the media file stored for use within your application.
GET https://www.linkedin.com/ambry/?x-li-ambry-ep=AQFBV...
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
Note
Use the content-type header in the response to indicate how the media data should be interpreted.
In a browser you can paste the mediaUrl and an active access token using the oauth2_access_token field to download the resume media.
https://www.linkedin.com/ambry/?x-li-ambry-ep=AQFBV...&oauth2_access_token=AQXsov...

Rows.Text: The access token of the application which received the mediaUrl.

Blocks.Text: If an application delivery is attempted and your system is unable to process, return the HTTP response and the associated errorCode and additionalErrorDetails in the response body to LinkedIn.
The following error codes can be returned:

Rows.Text: Responses are missing for the required questions.
The applicant will receive an application delivery failure email.

Input validation failed. For example, a phone number is entered in a format that the ATS doesn't accept, incorrect formatting or file type for attachments, or the size of an attachment exceeded the limit.
The applicant will receive an application delivery failure email.
A duplicate job application is received. This error only occurs if the applicationId of the incoming application matches that of an application that was already received.
The applicant will receive a successful delivery email.
The job posting is closed and cannot receive any more applications.
Disable onsite apply (LinkedIn Easy Apply) and redirect to apply url.
The applicant will receive an application delivery failure email.
Too many application submissions are being processed at the same time.
LinkedIn will retry to deliver the application. Once retries have been exhausted, the applicant will receive an application delivery failure email.
The signature from the job application failed to match with the partner's signature.
LinkedIn will not retry to deliver the application as this will be considered a fatal error.
An unknown error occurred on the ATS end. Only use this error when confident that the application should be retried after a short delay.
LinkedIn will retry to deliver the application. Once retries have been exhausted, the applicant will receive an application delivery failure email.
An error was caused by other unknown issues. This error should be sent by the partner when the error doesn't fall into the other predefined categories.
LinkedIn will retry to deliver the application. Once retries have been exhausted, the applicant will receive an application delivery failure email.
